comment: Building locations shown on site plan with overhead electric line on southern boundary. No building elevation sheets provided showing surveyed conductor elevations or roof/eave elevations. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained without these essential elevation views and dimension callouts.
applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings

comment: Overhead electric line documented on southern boundary. Building locations shown but no clearance dimensions provided. Cannot verify 15-foot radial clearance without dimension callouts, conductor identification (primary/secondary/neutral), and voltage specifications.
applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings relative to southern overhead line

comment: No building elevation sheets provided showing projections (overhangs, eaves, balconies, roofs, patios). Cannot verify required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections without elevation views.
applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings

comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents overhead utility line on-site along northern property boundary. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits northern overhead utilities with no demolition, relocation, or undergrounding notes. Cannot verify building setbacks from ROW and relocated facilities when existing utilities are not accounted for in proposed plan.
applicableAreas: Northern property boundary where overhead utilities exist on adjacent property and site

comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations or clearance dimensions to building faces and projections. This is a critical missing document type explicitly required by code to demonstrate vertical clearances from overhead electric conductors are met.
applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings

comment: No section or profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to building edges, projections, or other site features. Plans show buildings and overhead lines in plan view only with no cross-section documentation of vertical and horizontal relationships or clearance dimensions.
applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings relative to overhead lines

comment: Site plan shows proposed driveways crossing under overhead electric line on southern boundary. No vertical clearance dimensions provided on grading plan, profile sections, or utility plan. No determination whether truck traffic applies (16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement). No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data provided. Cannot verify driveways maintain minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead facilities including any telecommunications attachments.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing southern property boundary where overhead electric line exists

comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents overhead utility pole on-site along northern property boundary. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits this pole location with no notation regarding relocation, removal, or disposition. If pole remains and any site improvements (driveway, building, etc.) are within 30 feet of pole, relocation to minimum 30 feet from driveway edge is required. Current plan does not address pole conflicts.
applicableAreas: Northern property boundary where utility pole exists on existing conditions survey

comment: Plans show overhead lines but provide no clearance dimension callouts measuring distances from features to overhead conductors. Code requires clearance dimensions extend from outside conductor (not pole centerline or centerline of multi-conductor lines), yet no dimensions are provided to verify this measurement methodology. Cannot verify compliance when dimensions are completely absent.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimensions throughout site plan where overhead utilities exist

comment: Code establishes absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities (buildings, driveways, structures) under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, independent of clearance distances. Plans show driveways crossing under southern overhead line and buildings near overhead facilities. No explicit documentation confirms facilities are not placed directly beneath/over conductors. Cannot confirm compliance with absolute prohibition.
applicableAreas: Proposed buildings and driveways crossing overhead electric distribution facilities on southern boundary

comment: Building finished floor elevations range 686.25-685 ft MSL; overhead conductor elevations unknown. Without surveyed conductor heights and building roof elevations, vertical clearances cannot be verified and appear marginal. Code requires registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey and site-specific analysis when vertical clearance requirements may not be met. This critical survey and analysis are not provided despite marginal clearance conditions.
applicableAreas: All buildings and driveways where vertical clearance from overhead facilities appears marginal

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts proposed mitigation trees approximately 10-15 feet from southern overhead electric line. Code requires trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors be Utility Compatible species per ECM Appendix F (UC designation, generally mature height ≤20 feet). Specific tree species not confirmed on landscape plan. Cannot verify proposed trees are utility-compatible; if non-compatible species are planted, they will grow into overhead conductors, creating safety hazard.
applicableAreas: Proposed mitigation trees on southern property area within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors

comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries. Down guy wires and anchor locations are typically omitted from plans but are critical infrastructure. Site plan does not show any down guy wires, anchors, or associated clearances. If poles have down guys (common for distribution poles) and site improvements (driveways, accessible paths, buildings) are located near pole bases, guy anchors and cables could conflict with these features. Requires verification from Austin Energy and survey documentation.
applicableAreas: Utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries

comment: Easement exhibit (Sheet 2) and site plan do not show down guy anchor easements. Per Austin Energy transmission engineering standards, down guy anchors from distribution poles require dedicated 10-foot-wide easement extending minimum 5 feet past anchor ground entry point. If poles have down guys (typical for poles on property), required easements must be depicted on plat and easement exhibits. Missing easement documentation represents deficiency.
applicableAreas: Utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries if down guys are present

comment: No construction logistics, staging plan, or equipment operation zones provided on site plans. Code requires construction staging areas, equipment laydown zones, and work platforms maintain minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2. This is mandatory separate requirement from permanent clearances. Plans must include logistics plan or note addressing construction phase clearances from overhead lines.
applicableAreas: Entire site during construction phase

comment: Cover sheet and general notes do not include required notification regarding high-voltage work. Code requires plans to include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before any work begins near high-voltage overhead lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. This safety notification is mandatory when overhead electric facilities exist on or adjacent to site and construction is proposed.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet/general notes

comment: Trees are shown planted along the southern site boundary within approximately 5-10 feet of the overhead electric line (based on graphic scale 1"=20'). However, the landscape plan does not identify the species of these trees, so utility-compatible status per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified. Plant species schedule exists on Sheet 35 but is not cross-referenced to specific locations on the landscape plan. Provide species identification labels on the landscape plan for all trees proposed within 25 feet of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary of site, running parallel to overhead electric line

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) cannot be verified as meeting the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors because the landscape plan does not identify which species are planted at which locations. While Live Oak and Cedar Elm are shown in the plant schedule with 16-foot minimum heights, their mature heights per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified against specific planting locations on the site plan. Provide species identification and mature height notation on landscape plan for all proposed trees.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary of site, running parallel to overhead electric line; western street yard area near Valley View Road

comment: The landscape plan does not identify species of trees proposed near overhead electric facilities. Trees are shown with category symbols (M=Mitigation, SY=Street Yard, PL=Parking Lot) and geometric symbols but no botanical or common names are labeled on the plan. While a complete plant schedule exists on Sheet 35 listing Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, and Texas Mountain Laurel with quantities, this schedule is not cross-referenced to specific tree locations on the landscape plan. Add species common names or abbreviations (e.g., 'CE' for Cedar Elm, 'LO' for Live Oak) to tree symbols on the landscape plan for all trees within 50 feet of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Entire site, all proposed trees near overhead electric facilities

comment: The overhead electric line is shown on the landscape plan, but trees are not clearly related to it with dimensions. While both overhead electric lines and tree symbols are visible on Sheet 31, there are no dimension lines, call-outs, or notes indicating clearance distances between the trees and conductors. Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure separately from the landscape. Cross-reference the two plans with dimension lines or notes showing clearance distances between trees and overhead conductors, demonstrating compliance with 15-foot (distribution) and 50-foot (transmission) requirements.
applicableAreas: Entire site, particularly southern boundary and western boundary where trees and overhead electric lines overlap

comment: Transformer pad access door orientation is not indicated on the electrical plan. Without door orientation, the required 10-foot minimum clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure cannot be verified. The south pad is 5.9 feet from Building 7; if the access door faces this building, the 10-foot requirement would not be met.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

comment: No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in access paths or demonstrating clearances to any overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas associated with transformer locations. Vertical clearance compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

comment: Transformer easements are not shown on any of the site plan sheets. No easement boundaries or widths are depicted around the transformer pads to accommodate Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance requirements.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not labeled or dimensioned on the electrical plan. No reference callouts to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided. Compliance with AE Design pad specifications for the specified service type cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

comment: The transformer pad in the south area (near Building 7) is located 3.2 feet from the nearest vehicle circulation route, which is within the 4-foot threshold requiring bollard protection. No 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized bollards are shown on the electrical plan or any detail sheets. Bollards are required per AE Design equipment pad specifications.
applicableAreas: transformer pad in south area near Building 7
